subject: Telaris RFI: phased migration, canary strategy & validation runbook

Subject: Telaris RFI: migration phasing and canary validation

Hi Olga,

Thanks for taking our RFP. As part of our evaluation we need a detailed phased migration plan that explains the pilot, canary, and full cutover steps, plus the validation checks you'll run at each phase. Specifically we want:

- A timeline with milestone dates and estimated engineering effort (hours)
- Canary traffic percentages and duration for each step
- Monitoring hooks and success/failure criteria (SLOs, KPIs)
- Rollback triggers and expected recovery time
- Any data residency/ETL considerations during migration windows

I've attached a short questionnaire that our operations team uses (Telaris_RFI_phase_questions.xlsx). Priya (our integration consultant) will help coordinate the schedule.

Can you provide a draft plan by EOD next Tues? Also flag any questions now that might affect the timeline.

Thanks,
Sam Jenkins
VP of Platform Engineering
Telaris Systems

Sam —

Appreciate the questionnaire; received it and starting a draft. High level we propose the following approach (more detail below and in attached PDF):

1) Kickoff & discovery (1 week) — finalize integration points, auth, and data residency constraints
2) Pilot (2 weeks) — low-volume pilot with synthetic and real traffic; objective: validate request/response correctness, KV warmup, and latency SLOs
3) Canary ramp (3 stages over 2 weeks) — 1%, 10%, 30% traffic lanes with observability gates
4) Full cutover (planned weekend) — final sync and DNS switch with staged rollback windows

Quick asks that will affect timing:
- Do you have a hard blackout window for cutover weekend?
- Can we get a sample 48-hour traffic trace and a list of top request patterns?

I'm attaching our migration-phasing matrix (redwood_migration_phases_v1.pdf) and a pilot checklist. Will follow up with a full runbook draft early next week.

Best,

- Maintenance window: we have a preferred cutover weekend (Oct 9-10) but can be flexible by one week; raised internally.
- Traffic profile: we can provide the 48-hour sample by Tue EOD.

Sam / Olga —

Adding technical detail to the proposal Olga shared. Key items we will operate and monitor during pilot + canary:

Canary plan summary (recommended):
- Stage 1 (Pilot): 48–72h, ~0.5–1% production-equivalent traffic, sanity + correctness checks
- Stage 2 (Canary A): 7 days, 1% of real traffic, measure latency p95/p99, error rate (5xx)
- Stage 3 (Canary B): 7 days, 10% of traffic, run automated regression prompts set (provided by Telaris)
- Stage 4 (Canary C): 72h, 30% traffic, final stability window before full cutover

Observability & gates:
- Metrics to gate on: request success rate (>99.8%), 95th latency delta (<+15% vs baseline), token cost variance (<+10% expected)
- Monitoring hooks: Datadog dashboards + alert rules (link below) and a dedicated Slack incident channel
- Automated synthetic checks: prompt correctness suite (runs every 15m) and embedding similarity drift checks daily

Rollback & recovery:
- Immediate rollback trigger: sustained error rate >2% for 15 minutes OR latency p95 > baseline +50% for 10 minutes
- Expected RTO (rollback to previous serving variant): 5–15 minutes for routing rollback; full KV cold-start recovery 30–90 minutes depending on cache size

Integration points:
- Datadog and Sentry for monitoring; we will provide a guest Grafana read-only link during pilot
- API auth: OAuth2 with scoped keys; we recommend per-environment keys for pilot/canary/full

Docs / runbook: https://app.datadoghq.com/dashboard/redwood/telaris-metrics (Datadog dashboard)

I'm attaching a concise runbook (canary-runbook.md) with commands and rollback play actions. Happy to walk through this in a 30-min tech call.

— Rishi
Principal Technical Account Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachment: canary-runbook.md (markdown stub)

1) Can you confirm Redwood supports in-place prefix caching / KV warmup to reduce first-request latency?
2) For the 1% -> 10% -> 30% ramp, do you have automated traffic-splitting controls and a simple rollback API we can call from our deployment pipeline?
3) Is there an estimated ops-hours commitment from Redwood for pilot and each canary stage? (ballpark is fine)

We are aiming for the Oct 9-10 blackout window for full cutover; if we stick to that we'll need the pilot to start by Sep 20.

Sam

Sam / Priya / Rishi —

Attached is a consolidated plan that maps responsibilities, estimated hours, and milestone dates. Summary highlights:

Milestones (target):
- Discovery & kickoffs complete: Sep 3, 2026
- Pilot start (initial traffic): Sep 21, 2026 — 48–72h
- Canary ramp (1% -> 10%): Sep 28 — Oct 5, 2026
- Canary final (30%): Oct 6 — Oct 8, 2026
- Full cutover weekend: Oct 9 — Oct 10, 2026

Canary gating & ownership (high level):
- Redwood: provide runbook, run Datadog dashboards, operate traffic-split controls, respond to alerts (on-call)
- Telaris: run customer-side smoke tests, provide prompt/regression suites, sign off at each gate
- Bridge Consulting (Priya): coordinate schedule, validate data residency checks, lead cutover rehearsal

Estimated Redwood ops commitment (ballpark):
- Pilot: 24 person-hours (engineer + TAM support)
- Each canary stage: 16 person-hours per stage for active monitoring and runbook response
- Cutover weekend: 8–12 person-hours (on-call TAM + SRE support)

KV/prefix caching: Yes, Redwood supports prefix-based KV warmup and can pre-load frequently-used embeddings during pilot to reduce first-request latency. We'll include warmup scripts in canary-runbook.md.

Traffic-splitting & rollback: We expose programmatic traffic-split endpoints and a one-click rollback in the console; automated rollback can be triggered via API (we'll provide examples). Typical rollback to previous serving variant completes within 5–15 minutes, with full performance recovery ~30–90 minutes depending on cache sizes.

Next actions:
- Olga/Marissa: schedule a 30-min tech sync with Telaris + Bridge for Wed Sep 1.
- Telaris: share 48-hour traffic trace by Tue Aug 31.
- Contract: finalize SOW and DocuSign envelope (link below) so procurement can approve by Sep 10.
